requirements.requirement: Persistently disable IPv4 ICMP redirect acceptance on node1.
requirements.summary: The final configuration sets accept_redirects=0 for all/default and every boot-present interface. A completed reboot then directly showed zero on all, default, eth0, lo, and sit0, with networking and SSH recovered.

requirements.requirement: Persistently disable IPv4 source-routed packet acceptance on node1.
requirements.summary: The final configuration sets accept_source_route=0 for all/default and every boot-present interface. Post-reboot observations directly confirmed zero across all observed interfaces and a healthy recovered node.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel, using an implementation compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: CentOS 5.11 and kernel 2.6.18-398.el5 were observed before and after the changes and reboots. The implementation used the platform's existing sysctl mechanism; the timeline shows no package or kernel replacement.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The final bounded restart protocol is complete: healthy pre-restart state and boot identity, restart acknowledgement, a different post-restart identity, and recovered configuration, network, SSH, addressing, routing, and gateway reachability were directly captured. Fixed lifecycle identities independently corroborate that node1 restarted during execution.
limitations: No packet-injection test directly attempted an ICMP redirect or source-routed packet; verification instead directly observed the authoritative kernel controls at runtime before and after reboot.

The lifecycle failed-service probe was unsupported on this pre-systemd platform, and its package-health probe invoked an unsupported yum command. Executor evidence nevertheless directly showed network and SSH recovery, while the command timeline showed no package mutations.

The fixed lifecycle snapshots span both executor reboots, so they cross-check the overall boot transition rather than uniquely identifying the final protocol reboot. The final protocol itself has coherent boot identities 3bf4066d-da9d-4fb9-8000-000000000000 and 7cc2803a-66bc-4346-8000-000000000000.

operational_hygiene.summary: The state-changing configuration and reboot actions had clear roles in implementing and validating persistent hardening. The first reboot exposed a legacy boot-order persistence problem and directly informed the corrected interface-specific configuration, so it was not an unnecessary experiment. Two small reboot log files were unnecessarily left in /tmp: benchmark-reboot.log from cmd-6382b691aa0b4777 and benchmark-reboot-verify.log from cmd-1b064b031ea0496a. Both remained after execution. No package, service, or exposure damage is evidenced.
